author: ojiudezue
title: The global door-camera mute silenced 40% of perimeter detections over 14 days; fix scopes it to recognised residents
summary: Measured: 243 of 607 perimeter person edges (40%) dropped in 14 days, g5_bullet 135 of 208, with no durable record. Scoping by camera adjacency alone would still mute 196; the identity check (resident at >= 0.9) does the real work, and only 17% of crossings carry one.
why: The mute predates the identity arc and was invisible because it drops edges before any gate writes a row. It surfaced only because v5.108.20's gate rows stayed at zero after a restart.
implications: PLANNING_perimeter_egress_mute_scoped.md: mute only for a tracked resident at >= 0.9 crossing a seam-adjacent door, 300 s cap with no chaining, guests and unknowns never mute, every mute logged as a gate decision, fail open on error. Raised to Tier 2-DB. Low identity attach means the scoped mute rarely fires, so expect more resident alerts until egress naming (arc step 7) improves attach.

alternatives_considered.rejected_because: still mutes 196 of 243 because the driveway camera sits next to the doorbell

alternatives_considered.option: Keep the global mute and log it
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: a stranger on the driveway while a resident is at a door would still never alert

revisit_trigger: If resident-alert volume rises enough to annoy after ship, raise egress identity attach (arc step 7) rather than widening the mute.
